subject: botany
question_text: In case of polyembryony, if an embryo develops from the synergid and another from the nucellus, which is haploid and which is diploid?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.17, VSAQ 3). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book's answer lines ('Embryo develops from synergid is haploid', 'Embryo develops from nucellus is diploid') agree with this card; only the grammar is cleaned and the ploidy reasons added.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 2 marks

steps.label: Embryo from the synergid
lines: The embryo from the synergid is haploid (n).
A synergid is an unfertilised cell of the
embryo sac, so it carries only one set of
steps.why: Every cell of the embryo sac comes from the haploid megaspore by mitosis. A synergid is never fertilised, so an embryo built from it stays haploid.
common_mistakes: Calling the synergid embryo diploid because 'embryos are diploid' — this one skips fertilisation.
Giving the answer without the reason. The n/2n label alone reads as a guess.
steps.memory_tip: Inside the sac = haploid. No fusion happened in a synergid, so nothing doubled.
steps.margin_note: State n and add the one-line reason: the synergid is unfertilised.

steps.label: Embryo from the nucellus
lines: The embryo from the nucellus is diploid (2n).
The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the
ovule, so its cells have two chromosome sets.
steps.why: The nucellus belongs to the parent sporophyte, outside the embryo sac, so any embryo budding from it inherits the parent's diploid number.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two up. Fix the boundary: inside the embryo sac n, ovule tissue outside it 2n.
Writing 3n — that is the endosperm after triple fusion, not a nucellar embryo.
steps.memory_tip: Sac cells n, ovule body 2n. Synergid sits in the sac; nucellus is the ovule body.
steps.margin_note: The boxed pairing is the answer the examiner underlines — write both ploidies.

insider_note: This is really a boundary question: cells of the embryo sac are haploid, tissues of the ovule around it are diploid — say that boundary and both marks follow.
